focusSummary: Station survival signs (Eingang, Ausgang, Umsteigen), Austrian Bahnsteig vs. German Gleis, and Lego-style compound splitting from Haupt·bahn·hof up to Schienen·ersatz·verkehr.

lessonSteps.heading: The Lego Secret: Haupt·bahn·hof & Bahn·steig
lessonSteps.explanation: German doesn't invent obscure Latinate words for everyday infrastructure—it snaps tiny core roots together! Haupt ('main') + Bahn ('rail/track') + Hof ('courtyard/station') = der Hauptbahnhof ('main train station'). On Austrian ÖBB boards, your platform is der Bahn·steig ('rail-walkway'), whereas Deutsche Bahn (DB) in Germany displays das Gleis ('track').
lessonSteps.scenarioPrompt: You arrive at Wien Hauptbahnhof and check the overhead departure screen for your Salzburg train.
lessonSteps.nativeText: Wien Hauptbahnhof — Railjet nach Salzburg auf Bahnsteig 7.
lessonSteps.translation: Vienna Main Station — Railjet to Salzburg on Platform 7.
lessonSteps.usageTip: Read German compounds from right to left to find the core thing first: ein Hof ('station yard') -> ein Bahnhof ('rail station') -> der Hauptbahnhof ('the main rail station').

de-AT.nativeText: Wien Hauptbahnhof — Railjet nach Salzburg auf Bahnsteig 7.

de-DE.nativeText: München Hauptbahnhof — ICE nach Berlin auf Gleis 7.
de-DE.note: In Germany, departure boards and announcements say Gleis 7 ('Track 7') instead of ÖBB's Bahnsteig 7.

lessonSteps.regionalNote: DE: München Hauptbahnhof — ICE nach Berlin auf Gleis 7. (In Germany, departure boards and announcements say Gleis 7 ('Track 7') instead of ÖBB's Bahnsteig 7.)

lessonSteps.heading: Directional Prefixes: Ein·gang, Aus·gang & Um·steigen
lessonSteps.explanation: Once you know der Gang ('walkway / passage', from gehen) and steigen ('to step / climb'), three prefixes unlock every station corridor: Ein- ('in'), Aus- ('out'), and Um- ('around / transfer').
lessonSteps.scenarioPrompt: Following yellow overhead signs from the subway up to the regional train concourse.
lessonSteps.nativeText: Eingang zur U-Bahn · Ausgang zur Stadt · Umsteigen zum Regionalzug.
lessonSteps.translation: Entrance to the metro · Exit to the city · Transfer to the regional train.
lessonSteps.literalBreakdown: Ein·gang (in-way) · Aus·gang (out-way) · Um·steigen (transfer-stepping) · zum Regional·zug (to the regional-train)
lessonSteps.usageTip: Never confuse Ausgang ('way out / pedestrian exit') with Ausfahrt ('vehicle exit' on motorways and parking garages)!

lessonSteps.heading: Ticket Machines: der Fahr·karten·automat
lessonSteps.explanation: Red ÖBB touchscreens stand at every Austrian station: Fahr ('travel/ride') + Karten ('tickets/cards') + Automat ('machine') = der Fahrkartenautomat.Notice the linking -n- glue sound between Karte and Automat!
lessonSteps.scenarioPrompt: You look for a red ÖBB touchscreen kiosk in Innsbruck to print your mountain rail ticket.
lessonSteps.translation: Excuse me, where is the ÖBB ticket machine?
lessonSteps.literalBreakdown: Entschuldigung (excuse me) · wo ist (where is) · der Fahr·karten·automat (the travel-ticket-machine)
lessonSteps.usageTip: In Austria, die Fahrkarte (or das Ticket) is standard; in Switzerland you'll see das Billett.

de-DE.note: Identical compound in Germany (sometimes also called Ticketautomat at DB stations).

lessonSteps.regionalNote: DE: Entschuldigung, wo ist der Fahrkartenautomat? (Identical compound in Germany (sometimes also called Ticketautomat at DB stations).)

lessonSteps.heading: Taming 21-Letter Giants: Schienen·ersatz·verkehr
lessonSteps.explanation: Nothing intimidates travelers like seeing SCHIENENERSATZVERKEHR (often abbreviated SEV) flashing in orange on a platform screen—until you split its three Lego blocks: Schienen ('rails') + Ersatz ('replacement') + Verkehr ('traffic / transit service') = 'rail replacement bus service'!
lessonSteps.scenarioPrompt: Track maintenance closes a mountain line in Tyrol, and an orange SEV bus icon appears on screen.
lessonSteps.nativeText: Achtung: Schienenersatzverkehr mit Bus ab Vorplatz!
lessonSteps.translation: Attention: Rail replacement bus service departing from the station forecourt!
lessonSteps.literalBreakdown: Achtung (attention) · Schienen·ersatz·verkehr (rails-replacement-traffic) · mit Bus (by bus) · ab Vor·platz (from fore-plaza)
lessonSteps.usageTip: Whenever you see orange 'SEV' arrows painted on the floor at an Austrian or German station, follow them outside to the replacement coach—your regular train ticket is 100% valid!

drills.prompt: You see 'Schienenersatzverkehr (SEV)' on the departure board in Salzburg. Splitting Schienen · ersatz · verkehr tells you what?
options: Buses are replacing trains along this section of track
The dining car is serving hot breakfast
Only first-class tickets are valid today
This platform is an underground shopping mall
drills.correctAnswer: Buses are replacing trains along this section of track
drills.explanation: Schienen ('rails') + Ersatz ('replacement') + Verkehr ('traffic/service') decodes directly to 'rail replacement bus service'.

drills.prompt: On an Austrian ÖBB departure screen in Vienna, which word announces the platform number where you board your train?
drills.cue: ÖBB Austrian term (contrasted with DB's Gleis)
options: Bahnsteig
Sackerl
Schlagobers
Trinkgeld
drills.explanation: ÖBB stations across Austria announce platforms as Bahnsteig (e.g. Bahnsteig 4), whereas Deutsche Bahn in Germany announces Gleis 4.

drills.prompt: You just stepped off the Railjet and want to walk out into the city street. Which overhead sign do you follow?
options: Ausgang
Eingang
Fahrkartenautomat
Ruhezone
drills.explanation: Ausgang ('out-way') marks pedestrian exits to the street, whereas Eingang marks entrances.

gradedStories.title: Abenteuer am Wiener Hauptbahnhof
gradedStories.setting: 8:15 AM under the glass roof of Wien Hauptbahnhof before an Alpine day trip

paragraphs.nativeText: Leo steht früh am Morgen im großen Hauptbahnhof in Wien. Durch den Eingang strömen viele Reisende mit Koffern. Leo sucht zuerst den roten Fahrkartenautomat der ÖBB.
paragraphs.translation: Leo stands early in the morning inside the large main train station in Vienna. Many travelers with suitcases stream through the entrance. First Leo looks for the red ÖBB ticket machine.

paragraphs.nativeText: Er kauft eine Fahrkarte nach Salzburg und schaut auf die Anzeige: „Railjet um 8:30 Uhr auf Bahnsteig 8.“ Auf einer Nebenstrecke steht heute das lange Wort Schienenersatzverkehr, aber Leos Zug fährt pünktlich auf den Schienen!
paragraphs.translation: He buys a ticket to Salzburg and looks at the display board: 'Railjet at 8:30 AM on Platform 8.' On a branch line stands the long word Schienenersatzverkehr today, but Leo's train is running on time on the rails!

segments.regionalNote: In Austria, schauen is much more common in everyday speech than gucken (northern DE).
ÖBB (AT) uses Bahnsteig; DB (DE) uses Gleis.

paragraphs.nativeText: Leo muss heute nicht umsteigen. Er geht nicht zum Ausgang, sondern nimmt die Rolltreppe hinauf zu Bahnsteig 8.
paragraphs.translation: Leo doesn't have to transfer today. He doesn't walk to the exit, but takes the escalator up to Platform 8.

questions.question: Where does Leo buy his ticket to Salzburg?
options: At the red ÖBB ticket machine (Fahrkartenautomat)
Inside a coffeehouse next to the river
On a replacement bus
At the city exit
questions.explanation: Paragraph 1 & 2 explain that Leo finds 'den roten Fahrkartenautomat der ÖBB' and buys 'eine Fahrkarte nach Salzburg'.

questions.question: Does Leo's Salzburg Railjet require taking a replacement bus (Schienenersatzverkehr) or changing trains (umsteigen)?
options: Yes, he has to take three replacement buses
No—Schienenersatzverkehr is only on a branch line, and Leo's train runs direct and on time
Yes, he has to transfer twice at the exit
His train is canceled until tomorrow
questions.explanation: Schienenersatzverkehr applies only 'Auf einer Nebenstrecke' (on a branch line); Leo's Railjet runs on time on the rails and he 'muss heute nicht umsteigen'.

questions.question: How does Leo get up to Bahnsteig 8?
options: He walks out the Ausgang to the street
He takes the escalator (die Rolltreppe — Roll 'roll' + Treppe 'stairs')
He rides a bicycle
He waits at the Bankomat
questions.explanation: Paragraph 3 reads: 'sondern nimmt die Rolltreppe hinauf zu Bahnsteig 8.'

referenceSheets.title: German Transit & Menu Lego Roots
referenceSheets.subtitle: Master 10 high-leverage root blocks and unlock 50+ everyday station, street, and café compounds on sight

rows.meaning: Marks the primary hub, street, or course
rows.exampleNative: der Haupt·bahn·hof · die Haupt·straße · die Haupt·speise
rows.exampleTranslation: main train station · main street · main dish/entrée
rows.notes: Compare old literal meaning 'head' (preserved in 'die Hauptstadt' = capital city).

rows.exampleNative: die U-Bahn · die Straßen·bahn · die Berg·bahn
rows.exampleTranslation: underground metro · street-tram · mountain cable car
rows.notes: In Vienna, a tram is affectionately called die Bim (from its bell sound!).

rows.meaning: Raised boarding platform or mountain trail
rows.exampleNative: der Bahn·steig (AT) · der Steig · um·steigen · ein·steigen
rows.exampleTranslation: train platform · mountain path · to transfer · to board
rows.notes: ÖBB says Bahnsteig; DB in Germany says das Gleis.

rows.meaning: Anything tied to transit schedules, tickets, or vehicles
rows.exampleNative: die Fahr·karte · der Fahr·plan · die Ab·fahrt
rows.notes: Compare gehen/Gang (on foot) vs. fahren/Fahrt (on wheels/rails)!

rows.meaning: Pedestrian entrance, exit, train aisle, or meal course
rows.exampleNative: der Ein·gang · der Aus·gang · der Gang·platz
rows.notes: Contrast Gangplatz (aisle seat) with Fensterplatz (window seat).

rows.meaning: Backup bus, spare part, or dairy alternative
rows.exampleTranslation: rail replacement bus service · replacement train
rows.notes: Even borrowed into English ('ersatz')—in German it's completely neutral and practical!

rows.meaning: Public transit, regional lines, or road traffic
rows.exampleNative: der Nah·verkehr · der Fern·verkehr · der Stadt·verkehr
rows.exampleTranslation: local transit · long-distance rail · city transit
rows.notes: Notice linking -s- when Verkehr comes first: das Verkehr·s·mittel ('means of transport').

rows.meaning: Any printed or digital card, pass, or menu
rows.exampleNative: die Speise·karte · die Fahr·karte · die Bankomat·karte
rows.exampleTranslation: food menu · transit ticket · debit card (AT)
rows.notes: Die Weinkarte = wine list; die Tageskarte = day pass OR daily specials menu!

rows.meaning: Public city plaza or individual seat
rows.exampleNative: der Stephans·platz · der Sitz·platz · der Fenster·platz
rows.exampleTranslation: St. Stephen's Square · seat · window seat

rows.meaning: Dining cars, menus, starters, and desserts
rows.exampleNative: der Speise·wagen · die Vor·speise · die Nach·speise
rows.notes: Die Mehlspeise = quintessential Austrian sweet pastry/dessert course.
